statement: Let V be an (r+1)-dimensional complex vector subspace of C[x], r≥1. If every root of its monic Wronskian Wr_V is real, then V has a basis of polynomials with real coefficients. The conclusion allows multiple Wronskian roots.

answer.text: Let V be an (r+1)-dimensional complex vector subspace of C[x], r≥1. If every root of its monic Wronskian Wr_V is real, then V has a basis of polynomials with real coefficients. The conclusion allows multiple Wronskian roots.

notes:
This is the original Shapiro–Shapiro theorem. Its statement is reality of V; transversality of arbitrary osculating intersections is established in the subsequent MTV paper, Corollary 6.3.

scope: Polynomial subspaces of fixed dimension and degree bound with a prescribed Wronskian; Wronskian roots all real.
